ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is a flag composed of three horizontal stripes of equal height. The top stripe is divided into 4 equal parts, of which the 1st and 3rd parts are shaded, so the shading occupies 2/4. The middle stripe is divided into 3 equal parts, of which the left and right parts are shaded, so the shading occupies 2/3. The bottom stripe is divided into 2 equal parts, of which the left part is shaded, so the shading occupies 1/2. Then reason: The three stripes have equal height, so each stripe occupies 1/3 of the area of the whole flag. The shaded area proportion of the whole flag equals the average of the shaded proportions of the three stripes: (2/4 + 2/3 + 1/2) / 3 = (1/2 + 2/3 + 1/2) / 3 = (1 + 2/3) / 3 = (5/3) / 3 = 5/9.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the flag has three horizontal stripes of equal height. In the top stripe, 2 of the 4 equal sections are shaded; in the middle stripe, 2 of the 3 equal sections are shaded; in the bottom stripe, 1 of the 2 equal sections is shaded. From the text, use that all three stripes have equal height, so each stripe contributes one third of the total flag area. Compute the shaded fraction as the average of the shaded fractions in the three stripes: (2/4 + 2/3 + 1/2)/3 = 5/9.
